    11	/-!
    12	# The pointwise universal achiever over the total seed curve
    13	
    14	The seed-prime achiever is stated on a fibre curve over `κ(p)`.  The seed, however, is
    15	chosen pointwise on the total curve over the carve ring.  This file supplies the small
    16	reindexing bridge between the two statements: for a total point `z`, set
    17	`p := relCurveBasePoint C RZ z` and `z_fib := relCurveResiduePoint C RZ z`, then apply the
    18	seed-prime theorem at `(p, z_fib)`.
    19	
    20	There is one important topological qualification.  A total point can be the generic point
    21	of a vertical fibre, so `z_fib ≠ genericPoint (relCurve C κ(p))` is not true for every total
    22	point.  Accordingly the main theorem takes that hypothesis explicitly, while the companion
    23	dichotomy is unconditional and exposes the generic-fibre branch to downstream code.
    24	The old seed is left untouched.
    25	-/

   258	  have hM : ∀ ψ : relThetaSections C R π a,
   259	      relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) ψ
   260	        = (relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle :
   261	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
   262	          * relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) ψ :=
   263	    fun ψ => relThetaResSide_matching a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle ψ
   264	  -- eqn z |_W = (θ · c₂|_W) · eqn z' |_W
   265	  have h₁ : (relCurve C R).resHom
   266	        (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z)
   267	      = ((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle :
   268	            Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
   269	          * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right c₂)
   270	        * (relCurve C R).resHom
   271	            (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z') := by
   272	    calc (relCurve C R).resHom
   273	          (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z)
   274	        = relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) (D.sec z) := hF1
   275	      _ = (relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle :
   276	            Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
   277	          * relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) (D.sec z) :=
   278	        hM (D.sec z)
   279	      _ = (relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle :
   280	            Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
   281	          * ((relCurve C R).resHom
   282	              (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z')
   283	            * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right c₂) := by rw [hF4]
   284	      _ = ((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle :
   285	            Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
   286	          * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right c₂)
   287	          * (relCurve C R).resHom
   288	              (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z') := by
   289	        ring
   290	  -- eqn z' |_W = (θ⁻¹ · c₁|_W) · eqn z |_W
   291	  have hQ : relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) (D.sec z')
   292	      = (((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle)⁻¹ :
   293	            Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z')ˣ) :
   294	            Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
   295	        * relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) (D.sec z') := by
   296	    rw [Units.eq_inv_mul_iff_mul_eq]
   297	    exact (hM (D.sec z')).symm
   298	  have h₂ : (relCurve C R).resHom
   299	        (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z')
   300	      = ((((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle)⁻¹ :
   301	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z')ˣ) :
   302	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
   303	          * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left c₁)
   304	        * (relCurve C R).resHom
   305	            (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z) := by
   306	    calc (relCurve C R).resHom
   307	          (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z')
   308	        = relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) (D.sec z') := hF2
   309	      _ = (((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle)⁻¹ :
   310	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z')ˣ) :
   311	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
   312	          * relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) (D.sec z') := hQ
   313	      _ = (((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle)⁻¹ :
   314	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z')ˣ) :
   315	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
   316	          * ((relCurve C R).resHom
   317	              (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z)
   318	            * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left c₁) := by rw [hF3]
   319	      _ = ((((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle)⁻¹ :
   320	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z')ˣ) :
   321	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
   322	          * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left c₁)
   323	          * (relCurve C R).resHom
   324	              (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z) := by
   325	        ring
   326	  -- germwise regularity of the restricted equation
   327	  have hreg : ∀ (y : relCurve C R) (hy : y ∈ D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'),
   328	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z') y hy).hom
   329	        ((relCurve C R).resHom
   330	          (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z))
   331	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk y) := by
   332	    intro y hy
   333	    rw [show ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z') y hy).hom
   334	        ((relCurve C R).resHom
   335	          (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z))
   336	        = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z) y hy.1).hom (D.eqn z) from
   337	      TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply _ _ _ _ _]
   338	    exact D.germ_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors hD z hy.1
   339	  exact exists_unit_mul_of_mutual_dvd hreg h₁ h₂

   341	/-! ### The DDR-3 deliverable: the local-equation system and its adaptation -/
   342	
   343	variable (D)
   344	
   345	/-- **The local-equation system of a theta generator seed** (the DDR-3 family): the
   346	pieces are the pointed cover, the equations are the side components of the chosen
   347	generators; regularity is the germ-regularity law, the overlap units are the ratio
   348	law. -/
   349	noncomputable def localEquations [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator) :
   350	    (relCurve C R).LocalEquations where
   351	  cover := { opens := D.piece, mem_opens := D.mem_piece }
   352	  eqn := D.eqn
   353	  regular := fun z _ hy => D.germ_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors hD z hy
   354	  ratio_isUnit := fun z z' => D.exists_ratioUnit hD z z'
   355	
   356	@[simp]
   357	lemma localEquations_cover_opens [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator)
   358	    (z : relCurve C R) : (D.localEquations hD).cover.opens z = D.piece z := rfl
   359	
   360	@[simp]
   361	lemma localEquations_eqn [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator) (z : relCurve C R) :
   362	    (D.localEquations hD).eqn z = D.eqn z := rfl
   363	
   364	/-- **The finite chart adaptation of the seed's local-equation system**, through the
   365	DD-1 extraction (`exists_divisorAdaptation`); no anchor field of `DivisorAdaptation` is
   366	consumed here (DD-2 carrier-surgery freeze discipline). -/
   367	noncomputable def divisorAdaptation [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator) :
   368	    DivisorAdaptation C R π (D.localEquations hD) :=
   369	  (exists_divisorAdaptation C R π (D.localEquations hD)).some
   370	
   371	/-! ### The divisibility laws for DDR-4/DDR-5 -/
   372	
   373	/-- **The stalk ideal of the constructed system is spanned by the seed equation** at the
   374	tautological covering member. -/
   375	lemma stalkIdeal_localEquations [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator)
   376	    (z : relCurve C R) :
   377	    (D.localEquations hD).stalkIdeal z
   378	      = Ideal.span {((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z) z (D.mem_piece z)).hom
   379	          (D.eqn z)} := rfl
   380	
   381	/-- **The germ divisibility law**: at any point `y` of the piece of `z`, the germ of the
   382	side component of every element of `K` lies in the span of the germ of the equation. -/
   383	theorem germ_relThetaResSide_mem_span [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator)
   384	    (z : relCurve C R) {ψ : relThetaSections C R π a} (hψ : ψ ∈ K)
   385	    {y : relCurve C R} (hy : y ∈ D.piece z) :
   386	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z) y hy).hom
   387	        (relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) ψ)
   388	      ∈ Ideal.span
   389	        {((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z) y hy).hom (D.eqn z)} := by
   390	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Ideal.mem_span_singleton.mp (hD.dvd z hψ)
   391	  rw [hc, map_mul]
   392	  exact Ideal.mul_mem_right _ _ (Ideal.subset_span rfl)
   393	
   394	/-- **The vanishing law (the DDR-5 containment half)**: every element of `K` vanishes
   395	along the constructed local-equation system — `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ − d))` in the DD-4 spelling
   396	`Scheme.LocalEquations.vanishingSubmodule`. -/
   397	theorem le_vanishingSubmodule [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator) :
   398	    K ≤ (D.localEquations hD).vanishingSubmodule R
   399	      (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁
   400	      (relThetaCocycle C R π a) := by
   401	  intro ψ hψ
   402	  rw [Scheme.LocalEquations.mem_vanishingSubmodule_iff]
   403	  constructor
   404	  · -- chart-0 component
   405	    intro z hz
   406	    have hz₀ : z ∈ relPinnedChart C R π false := hz.2
   407	    -- work on the overlap of the piece of `z` with the pinned chart 0
   408	    have hWle : D.piece z ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π false
   409	        ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z) ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π false :=
   410	      inf_le_inf (D.piece_le z) le_rfl

    42	/-- Multiply a seed's existing cutter by a second point-containing chart section. -/
    43	noncomputable def productCutter (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)
    44	    (c : ∀ z : relCurve C R, Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)))
    45	    (hc : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (c z)) :

    60	/-- Multiplying an ann-cutter by a seed whose fibre nonvanishing is already known preserves
    61	both inputs of `isGenerator_of_ann_cutter`. -/
    62	theorem isGenerator_productCutter (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)
    63	    (c : ∀ z : relCurve C R, Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)))
    64	    (hc : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (c z))
    65	    (hann : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) ⦃ψ : relThetaSections C R π a⦄, ψ ∈ K →
    66	      c z * relThetaResSide a (D.side z) le_rfl ψ
    67	        ∈ Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a (D.side z) le_rfl (D.sec z)})
    68	    (hfib : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) (p : PrimeSpectrum R),
    69	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).basicOpen
    70	          (relPinnedSectionsMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField π (D.side z) (D.h z)) :
    71	        (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).Opens) ≠ ⊥ →
    72	      relPinnedSectionsMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField π (D.side z)
    73	        (relThetaResSide a (D.side z) le_rfl (D.sec z)) ≠ 0) :
    74	    (productCutter D c hc).IsGenerator := by
    75	  apply isGenerator_of_ann_cutter (productCutter D c hc)
    76	  · intro z ψ hψ
    77	    dsimp only [productCutter]
    78	    simpa only [mul_assoc, mul_left_comm, mul_comm] using
    79	      (Ideal.mul_mem_left _ (D.h z) (hann z hψ))
    80	  · intro z p hne
    81	    apply hfib z p
    82	    intro hbot
    83	    apply hne
    84	    change (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).basicOpen
    85	        (relPinnedSectionsMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField π (D.side z)
    86	          (c z * D.h z)) = ⊥
    87	    rw [(relPinnedSectionsMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField π (D.side z)).map_mul,
    88	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).basicOpen_mul, hbot, inf_bot_eq]
    89

    63	/-! ## The theta generator seed and the `lm:ctn` clauses -/
    64	
    65	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    66	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    67	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}
    68	
    69	/-- **A theta generator seed for a submodule `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))`** (worksheet §3.4.1): at
    70	every point `z` of the relative curve, a pinned chart side containing `z`, a basic-open
    71	neighbourhood piece `D(h z)` of the chart, and a global section `sec z ∈ K` — the
    72	candidate local generator.  The two `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed are
    73	`ThetaGeneratorSeed.IsGenerator`. -/
    74	structure ThetaGeneratorSeed (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    75	    [Algebra k R] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (a : ℕ)
    76	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) : Type u where
    77	  /-- The pinned chart side of the piece at `z`. -/
    78	  side : relCurve C R → Bool
    79	  /-- The basic-open generator of the piece at `z`. -/
    80	  h : ∀ z : relCurve C R, Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π (side z))
    81	  /-- The point lies in its piece. -/
    82	  mem_basicOpen : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (h z)
    83	  /-- The candidate local generator at `z`. -/
    84	  sec : relCurve C R → relThetaSections C R π a
    85	  /-- The candidate generators are drawn from `K`. -/
    86	  sec_mem : ∀ z, sec z ∈ K
    87	
    88	namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed
    89	
    90	variable {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)
    91	
    92	/-- The neighbourhood piece at `z`: the basic open `D(h z)` of the pinned chart. -/
    93	noncomputable def piece (z : relCurve C R) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
    94	  (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h z)
    95	
    96	lemma mem_piece (z : relCurve C R) : z ∈ D.piece z := D.mem_basicOpen z
    97	
    98	lemma piece_le (z : relCurve C R) : D.piece z ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z) :=
    99	  (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h z)
   100	
   101	/-- The pieces are affine (basic opens of the affine pinned charts). -/
   102	lemma isAffineOpen_piece (z : relCurve C R) : IsAffineOpen (D.piece z) :=
   103	  (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)).basicOpen (D.h z)
   104	
   105	/-- **Flatness of the piece sections over the test ring** (the (iii)⟹(i) licence). -/
   106	theorem flat_sections_piece (z : relCurve C R) :

    25	extraction: an adaptation always exists, whereas the colength certificate is an extra

    62	  set e₁ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₁) ≃ ι₁ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₁).symm with he₁

    68	      h₁ := fun j => f₁ (e₁ j)

    70	      a₁ := fun j => b₁ (e₁ j)

122 /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon-inbox/SKILL.md
---
name: horizon-inbox
description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter agent-ready items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create, and message other projects via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
---

The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
fields.

## Read

- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
  or `project:<name>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience).
  Scope/project says what the item is about.
- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, and items addressed
  to its project. It should ignore other projects' addressed items.
- Kinds: `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).

## Act

Authorship is automatic: every item and comment you create through the CLI is
attributed to your role (normally `horizon`) from the run environment — you do
**not** pass `--author` (a stray `--author work-reviewer` is demoted to the
`agent` metadata, not used as the author, so the author set stays conventional).
If you are a dispatched **subagent**, add `--agent <your-name>` (e.g. `--agent
work-reviewer`) to record your identity; it is stored in metadata and shown
next to the role in the UI, keeping the author itself a clean role. Items and
comments are also auto-tagged with the run/session provenance (a small chip in the
UI); you do not pass this yourself.

New inbox items use a two-part body:

- First paragraph = concise title. Keep it short enough to scan in one UI row
  (aim for under ~100 characters); do not put the full explanation here.
- Second paragraph and later = non-empty description. Put the evidence, impact,
  next action, and relevant ids/files here. The description is **mandatory** — an
  item that is only a title is rejected.

Write bodies and comments in **Markdown**: the dashboard renders it. Use short
paragraphs and `-` bullet lists instead of one wall-of-text paragraph, `**bold**`
for the key claim, and backticks for ids, lemma names, files, and code
(`` `lem:foo` ``, `` `Foo.lean:42` ``). A long unstructured blob is hard to scan.

Do not create an item whose body is only a title. If you need a `[persistent]` or
`[temporary]` tag, put it at the start of the title paragraph and keep the rest
of that paragraph concise.

Before opening a new item, search the open inbox for the same topic using
`horizon inbox list --status open --query "key words" --json` and, when relevant,
`--project P` / `--to R`. If a live item already covers the same issue, do not
open a duplicate: add a comment with the new evidence, or edit the body if the
main description is stale. If you discover an open item is obsolete, already
solved, consumed, or superseded, add a short comment when the reason is not
obvious and then run `horizon inbox archive <id>`.

- `horizon inbox comment <id> --body "..."` — progress note on an item (record
  what you did; not to ask the human for clarification). Do not write your name
  into the comment body; the author is set automatically. Drop a comment at each **key advance**
  while you work an item (a milestone reached, a route ruled out, a blocker hit),
  not only at the end — these comments are the item's visible progress trail.
- **Write comments as mathematics, for a human.** State the key step that
  succeeded in human-readable mathematical language (LaTeX for formulas), naming
  the result and the idea — e.g. "Proved $H^i(X,\mathcal{F})=0$ for $i>\dim X$ by
  reducing to the affine case via Čech cohomology." Mention Lean declaration
  names and file paths only as supporting detail; the substance is the maths, not
  a code changelog. This applies to comments on **roadmap items and tasks** too:
  when a key step lands, record it there in the same mathematical, legible style.
- `horizon inbox archive <id>` — soft-delete: keep the item for the record but
  hide it from the dashboard by default. Use for stale, superseded, consumed, or
  no-longer-key context. Keeping the inbox tidy this way is your job (or the
  janitor subagent's) — prune memory/info so they remain small.
- `horizon inbox complete <id>` — mark an item resolved only when it records work
  you genuinely concluded and want to keep visible outside the archive. Before
  completing, add a short **conclusion comment**: first the mathematical
  conclusion (what was proved/established, in words + LaTeX), then concise
  metadata (runs, approximate LOC, files/declarations involved). A reader should
  grasp the result and how it was concluded without opening the logs.
- `horizon inbox add --body "Short title\n\nDescription with details and next action." [--to R] [--project P] [--persistent|--temporary] [--agent <name> if a subagent]`
  — open a new item.
  - `--to` is the recipient: `horizon`, `human`, or `project:<name>`.
    Use `--to project:<name>` to message another project (e.g. "I rewrote your
    `foo` declaration more cleanly, you may want it").
  - `--project` says what the item is ABOUT (its subject).
  - `--persistent` / `--temporary` just prepend a `[persistent]` / `[temporary]`
    tag to the body.
  - `--pending` labels the item `not-ready` instead of the default `agent-ready`,
    so it stays invisible to agents until a human releases it.
- `horizon inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body "Short memory title\n\nDurable fact, convention, or dead end."` — record a durable
  note / dead end. Memory lives in the inbox, so it is rendered in the "Memory"
  section and a human can prune it like any other item.
- `horizon inbox protect --body "..." [--project P] [--file F] [--declaration D] [--blueprint-node N]`
  — add a semantic standing constraint the Horizon agent must respect (a soft freeze),
  e.g. "do not change the signature of `Foo.bar`". These render as a
  "Protected" section; honour them, including semantic ones. For a target that
  must be mechanically blocked before dispatch, the user uses the config-backed
  `horizon freeze add <file|declaration|blueprint-node> <target>` command instead.

Reading convention: an item tagged `[persistent]` is a standing rule — respect
it every round and keep it open while relevant. `[temporary]` (or untagged) is
one-shot — archive it once consumed. Items in the "Protected" section are never
modified.

    27	  finiteness/projectivity transfers.

    29	  prime `p` of `R`, `rankAtStalk M p = rankAtStalk A p`.  Route (the semilocal
    30	  Pic-vanishing): the fibre algebra `κ(p) ⊗[R] A` is a finite algebra over the residue
    31	  field, hence artinian, hence semilocal, so its Picard group is trivial (mathlib) and
    32	  the fibre of `M` — an invertible module over the fibre algebra — is **free of rank
    33	  one**; taking `κ(p)`-dimensions gives the claim through `Module.rankAtStalk_eq`.
    34	
    35	The DD-4 consumer instantiates this at `A := ` the glued equalizer algebra of a certified
    36	divisor family (with `Module.Finite`/`Projective`/`rankAtStalk = g` from the certificate
    37	clause (c2)) and `M := ` the Θ-twisted glued module `W(d)^{Θᵃ}`
    38	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyThetaRank`).
    39	-/

    49	/-- **Projectivity is transitive**: if `A` is a projective `R`-module and `P` is a
    50	projective `A`-module, then `P` is projective as an `R`-module.  The `A`-splitting
    51	`P →ₗ[A] (P →₀ A)` provided by `Module.projective_def'` restricts to an `R`-splitting,
    52	and `P →₀ A` is a projective `R`-module (a direct sum of copies of `A`, through
    53	`finsuppLequivDFinsupp`). -/
    54	theorem Module.Projective.trans {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (A : Type v) [CommRing A]
    55	    [Algebra R A] {P : Type*} [AddCommMonoid P] [Module A P] [Module R P]
    56	    [IsScalarTower R A P] [Module.Projective R A] [Module.Projective A P] :
    57	    Module.Projective R P := by
    58	  classical
    59	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := Module.projective_def'.mp ‹Module.Projective A P›
    60	  haveI : Module.Projective R (P →₀ A) :=
    61	    Module.Projective.of_equiv (finsuppLequivDFinsupp (R := R) (M := A) (ι := P)).symm
    62	  exact Module.Projective.of_split
    63	    (LinearMap.restrictScalars R s)
    64	    (LinearMap.restrictScalars R (Finsupp.linearCombination A _root_.id))
    65	    (LinearMap.ext fun p => DFunLike.congr_fun hs p)

    73	section BaseChangeAlgebraModule
    74	
    75	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    76	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    77	variable (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower R A M]
    78	
    79	/-- The `S`-linear structure map `M →ₗ[R] (S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M`, `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`. -/
    80	noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit : M →ₗ[R] (S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M :=
    81	  LinearMap.restrictScalars R (TensorProduct.mk A (S ⊗[R] A) M 1)
    82	
    83	@[simp]
    84	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit_apply (m : M) :
    85	    baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit S A M m = (1 : S ⊗[R] A) ⊗ₜ[A] m := rfl
    86	
    87	/-- (Implementation) The collapse pairing `(S ⊗[R] A) →ₗ[R] M →ₗ[R] S ⊗[R] M`,
    88	`(s ⊗ a, m) ↦ s ⊗ (a • m)`, obtained by currying the composite of the associator with
    89	the `A`-action collapse on the right factor. -/
    90	noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing :
    91	    (S ⊗[R] A) →ₗ[R] M →ₗ[R] S ⊗[R] M :=
    92	  TensorProduct.curry
    93	    ((LinearMap.lTensor S
    94	        ((LinearMap.liftBaseChange A (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[R] M)).restrictScalars R)) ∘ₗ
    95	      (TensorProduct.assoc R S A M).toLinearMap)
    96	
    97	@[simp]
    98	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul (s : S) (a : A) (m : M) :
    99	    baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M (s ⊗ₜ[R] a) m = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a • m) := by
   100	  simp [baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing]
   101	
   102	/-- The `A`-action on `S ⊗[R] A` through `Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra`, on pure
   103	tensors. -/
   104	lemma rightAlgebra_smul_tmul (a : A) (s : S) (b : A) :
   105	    a • (s ⊗ₜ[R] b) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a * b) := by
   106	  change ((1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] a) * (s ⊗ₜ[R] b) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a * b)
   107	  rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, one_mul]
   108	
   109	/-- (Implementation) The pairing is `A`-balanced. -/
   110	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_smul (a : A) (x : S ⊗[R] A) (m : M) :
   111	    baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M (a • x) m
   112	      = baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M x (a • m) := by
   113	  induction x with
   114	  | zero => simp
   115	  | tmul s b =>
   116	      rw [rightAlgebra_smul_tmul, baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul,
   117	        baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul, mul_smul, smul_comm]
   118	  | add x y hx hy => rw [smul_add, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, hx, hy, map_add,
   119	      LinearMap.add_apply]
   120	
   121	/-- (Implementation) The pairing is `S`-semilinear in the first slot. -/
   122	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_smul_left (c : S) (x : S ⊗[R] A) (m : M) :
   123	    baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M (c • x) m
   124	      = c • baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M x m := by
   125	  induction x with
   126	  | zero => simp
   127	  | tmul s b =>
   128	      rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul,
   129	        baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul, TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul]
   130	  | add x y hx hy => rw [smul_add, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, hx, hy, map_add,
   131	      LinearMap.add_apply, smul_add]
   132	
   133	/-- (Implementation) The additive collapse `(S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M →+ S ⊗[R] M`. -/
   134	noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse :
   135	    (S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M →+ S ⊗[R] M :=
   136	  TensorProduct.liftAddHom
   137	    { toFun := fun x =>
   138	        { toFun := fun m => baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M x m
   139	          map_zero' := by simp
   140	          map_add' := fun m n => by simp }
   141	      map_zero' := by ext m; simp
   142	      map_add' := fun x y => by ext m; simp }
   143	    (fun a x m => baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_smul S A M a x m)
   144	
   145	@[simp]
   146	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul (x : S ⊗[R] A) (m : M) :
   147	    baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse S A M (x ⊗ₜ[A] m)
   148	      = baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M x m := rfl
   149	
   150	/-- **The base-change collapse**: for an `A`-module `M` and an `R`-algebra `S`, the
   151	base change of `M` along `A → S ⊗[R] A` is the base change along `R → S`,
   152	`S`-linearly: `(S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] M` on generators
   153	`(s ⊗ a) ⊗ m ↦ s ⊗ (a • m)`. -/
   154	noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraModule : (S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] M where
   155	  toFun := baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse S A M
   156	  map_add' := map_add _
   157	  map_smul' := by
   158	    intro c z
   159	    rw [RingHom.id_apply]
   160	    induction z with
   161	    | zero => simp
   162	    | tmul x m =>
   163	        rw [show c • (x ⊗ₜ[A] m) = (c • x) ⊗ₜ[A] m from TensorProduct.smul_tmul' c x m,
   164	          baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul, baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul,
   165	          baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_smul_left]
   166	    | add z w hz hw =>
   167	        rw [smul_add, map_add, map_add, hz, hw, smul_add]
   168	  invFun := LinearMap.liftBaseChange S (baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit S A M)
   169	  left_inv := by
   170	    intro z
   171	    induction z with
   172	    | zero => simp
   173	    | tmul x m =>
   174	        rw [baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul]
   175	        induction x with
   176	        | zero => simp [TensorProduct.zero_tmul]
   177	        | tmul s b =>
   178	            rw [baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul, LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul,
   179	              baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit_apply]
   180	            calc s • ((1 : S ⊗[R] A) ⊗ₜ[A] (b • m))
   181	                = s • (b • ((1 : S ⊗[R] A) ⊗ₜ[A] m)) := by
   182	                  rw [TensorProduct.tmul_smul]
   183	              _ = s • ((b • (1 : S ⊗[R] A)) ⊗ₜ[A] m) := by
   184	                  rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul' b _ m]
   185	              _ = (s • b • (1 : S ⊗[R] A)) ⊗ₜ[A] m := TensorProduct.smul_tmul' s _ m
   186	              _ = (s ⊗ₜ[R] b) ⊗ₜ[A] m := by
   187	                  congr 1
   188	                  rw [show b • (1 : S ⊗[R] A) = (1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] (b * 1) from
   189	                    rightAlgebra_smul_tmul S A b 1 1, mul_one, TensorProduct.smul_tmul',
   190	                    smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
   191	        | add x y hx hy =>
   192	            rw [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, map_add, hx, hy, TensorProduct.add_tmul]
   193	    | add z w hz hw =>
   194	        rw [map_add, map_add, hz, hw]
   195	  right_inv := by
   196	    intro z
   197	    induction z with
   198	    | zero => simp
   199	    | tmul s m =>
   200	        rw [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul, baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit_apply,
   201	          TensorProduct.smul_tmul' s _ m, baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul,
   202	          show s • (1 : S ⊗[R] A) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : A) by
   203	            rw [show (1 : S ⊗[R] A) = (1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : A) from rfl,
   204	              TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one],
   205	          baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul, one_smul]
   206	    | add z w hz hw => rw [map_add, map_add, hz, hw]
   207	
   208	@[simp]
   209	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModule_tmul_tmul (s : S) (a : A) (m : M) :
   210	    baseChangeAlgebraModule S A M ((s ⊗ₜ[R] a) ⊗ₜ[A] m) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a • m) := by
   211	  change baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse S A M ((s ⊗ₜ[R] a) ⊗ₜ[A] m) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a • m)
   212	  rw [baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul, baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul]
   213	
   214	end BaseChangeAlgebraModule

   250	/-- (Implementation) The fibre algebra `κ(p) ⊗[R] A` of a finite `R`-algebra is
   251	semilocal: it is a finite algebra over the residue field, hence artinian. -/
   252	theorem finite_maximalSpectrum_fiber (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
   253	    Finite (MaximalSpectrum (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] A)) := by
   254	  haveI : IsArtinianRing (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] A) := by

   257	    exact isArtinian_of_tower p.asIdeal.ResidueField inferInstance
   258	  infer_instance

   260	/-- **The rank transfer** (the semilocal Pic-vanishing): an invertible module over a
   261	finite projective `R`-algebra `A` has the same rank as `A` at every prime of `R`.
   262	Route: `rankAtStalk` is the fibre dimension (`Module.rankAtStalk_eq`); the fibre
   263	`κ(p) ⊗[R] M ≃ (κ(p) ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M` is an invertible module over the fibre algebra,
   264	which is artinian (hence semilocal), so its Picard group is trivial and the fibre is
   265	free of rank one over the fibre algebra. -/
   266	theorem rankAtStalk_eq_of_module_finite (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
   267	    Module.rankAtStalk M p = Module.rankAtStalk A p := by
   268	  haveI : Module.Finite R M := finite_trans (A := A)
   269	  haveI : Module.Projective R M := projective_trans (A := A)
   270	  haveI : Module.Flat R M := Module.Flat.of_projective
   271	  haveI : Module.Flat R A := Module.Flat.of_projective
   272	  rw [Module.rankAtStalk_eq, Module.rankAtStalk_eq]
   273	  set κ := p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   274	  -- the fibre algebra and the fibre of `M` over it
   275	  set Aκ := κ ⊗[R] A with hAκ
   276	  haveI : Finite (MaximalSpectrum Aκ) := finite_maximalSpectrum_fiber (A := A) p
   277	  -- the fibre of `M` as a base change over `A`, an invertible `Aκ`-module
   278	  haveI hinv : Module.Invertible Aκ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) := inferInstance
   279	  haveI : Module.Free Aκ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) := inferInstance
   280	  obtain ⟨e⟩ : Nonempty ((Aκ ⊗[A] M) ≃ₗ[Aκ] Aκ) :=
   281	    Module.Invertible.free_iff_linearEquiv.mp ‹_›
   282	  -- transport dimensions along the collapse and the rank-one equivalence
   283	  have h1 : Module.finrank κ (κ ⊗[R] M) = Module.finrank κ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) :=
   284	    (TensorProduct.baseChangeAlgebraModule κ A M).symm.finrank_eq
   285	  have h2 : Module.finrank κ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) = Module.finrank κ Aκ :=
   286	    (e.restrictScalars κ).finrank_eq
   287	  change Module.finrank κ (κ ⊗[R] M) = Module.finrank κ (κ ⊗[R] A)
   288	  rw [h1, h2]
   289

   181	nonzerodivisors at every point of the pulled cover members. Each point lies in a piece;
   182	there the pulled equation differs from the pulled piece equation — regular by
   183	`pulledEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors` + the affine germ seam — by a stalk unit assembled from
   184	the adaptation unit and the transition unit of `d`. -/
   185	theorem germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   186	    (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j))
   187	    (y z : relCurve C R')
   188	    (hz : z ∈ (d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y) :
   189	    ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ
   190	        ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y) z hz).hom
   191	        (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R R') d y)
   192	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R').presheaf.stalk z) := by
   193	  obtain ⟨j, hzj⟩ := (A.toFinCoverData.baseChange R').exists_mem_pieces z
   194	  -- the point below `z` and its memberships
   195	  have hzj' : z ∈ relCurveMap C R R' ⁻¹ᵁ A.pieces j := by
   196	    rw [← A.toFinCoverData.pieces_baseChange R' j]
   197	    exact hzj
   198	  have hfzj : (relCurveMap C R R').base z ∈ A.pieces j := hzj'
   199	  have hfzy : (relCurveMap C R R').base z ∈ d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y) :=
   200	    hz
   201	  have hfzW : (relCurveMap C R R').base z ∈
   202	      A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y) :=
   203	    ⟨hfzj, hfzy⟩
   204	  -- the regular germ of the pulled piece equation
   205	  have hF : ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ
   206	      ((A.toFinCoverData.baseChange R').pieces j) z hzj).hom (A.pulledEqn R' j) ∈
   207	      nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R').presheaf.stalk z) :=
   208	    IsAffineOpen.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   209	      ((A.toFinCoverData.baseChange R').isAffineOpen_pieces j)
   210	      (A.pulledEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors R' hproj j) z hzj
   211	  -- germ of the pulled piece equation = stalk image of the germ of the piece equation
   212	  have hgermF : ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ
   213	      ((A.toFinCoverData.baseChange R').pieces j) z hzj).hom (A.pulledEqn R' j) =
   214	      ((relCurveMap C R R').stalkMap z).hom
   215	        (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j)
   216	          ((relCurveMap C R R').base z) hfzj).hom (A.eqn j)) := by
   217	    have happ := (relCurveMap C R R').germ_stalkMap_apply (A.pieces j) z hfzj (A.eqn j)
   218	    -- `pulledEqn = res (app (eqn))`, so its germ over the piece is the germ of
   219	    -- `app (eqn)` over the preimage
   220	    have hres : ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ
   221	        ((A.toFinCoverData.baseChange R').pieces j) z hzj).hom (A.pulledEqn R' j) =
   222	        ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ
   223	          (relCurveMap C R R' ⁻¹ᵁ A.pieces j) z hzj').hom
   224	          (((relCurveMap C R R').app (A.pieces j)).hom (A.eqn j)) := by
   225	      have hle : (A.toFinCoverData.baseChange R').pieces j ≤
   226	          relCurveMap C R R' ⁻¹ᵁ A.pieces j :=
   227	        A.toFinCoverData.baseChange_pieces_le_preimage R' j
   228	      have := TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply (relCurve C R').presheaf
   229	        (homOfLE hle) z hzj (((relCurveMap C R R').app (A.pieces j)).hom (A.eqn j))
   230	      rw [← this]
   231	      rfl
   232	    rw [hres, happ]
   233	  -- decompose the germ of the piece equation through the pointwise unit clause of the
   234	  -- adaptation at the base point of `y`
   235	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j ((relCurveMap C R R').base y)
   236	  have hdecomp : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j)
   237	      ((relCurveMap C R R').base z) hfzj).hom (A.eqn j) =
   238	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   239	          (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))
   240	          ((relCurveMap C R R').base z) hfzW).hom
   241	        (u : Γ(relCurve C R,
   242	          A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))) *
   243	        ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   244	          (d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))
   245	          ((relCurveMap C R R').base z) hfzy).hom
   246	          (d.eqn ((relCurveMap C R R').base y)) := by
   247	    have hkey := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   248	        (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))
   249	        ((relCurveMap C R R').base z) hfzW).hom hu
   250	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at hkey
   251	    exact hkey
   252	  -- the goal germ is the stalk image of the germ of `d.eqn (f.base y)`
   253	  have hgermG : ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ
   254	      ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y) z hz).hom
   255	      (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R R') d y) =
   256	      ((relCurveMap C R R').stalkMap z).hom
   257	        (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   258	          (d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))
   259	          ((relCurveMap C R R').base z) hfzy).hom
   260	          (d.eqn ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))) := by
   261	    rw [Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn]
   262	    have happLE : ((relCurveMap C R R').appLE
   263	        (d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))
   264	        ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y) le_rfl).hom
   265	        (d.eqn ((relCurveMap C R R').base y)) =
   266	        ((relCurve C R').presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_refl
   267	          ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y))).op).hom
   268	          (((relCurveMap C R R').app
   269	            (d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))).hom
   270	            (d.eqn ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))) := rfl
   271	    rw [happLE, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
   272	    exact ((relCurveMap C R R').germ_stalkMap_apply
   273	      (d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y)) z hfzy
   274	      (d.eqn ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))).symm
   275	  -- assemble: the pulled piece equation's germ is a unit multiple of the goal germ
   276	  have hunit : IsUnit (((relCurveMap C R R').stalkMap z).hom
   277	      (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   278	        (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))
   279	        ((relCurveMap C R R').base z) hfzW).hom
   280	        (u : Γ(relCurve C R,
   281	          A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))))) :=
   282	    (u.isUnit.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   283	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))
   284	      ((relCurveMap C R R').base z) hfzW).hom).map
   285	      ((relCurveMap C R R').stalkMap z).hom
   286	  have hkey : ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ
   287	      ((A.toFinCoverData.baseChange R').pieces j) z hzj).hom (A.pulledEqn R' j) =
   288	      (hunit.unit : ((relCurve C R').presheaf.stalk z)ˣ) *
   289	        (((relCurveMap C R R').stalkMap z).hom
   290	          (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   291	            (d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))
   292	            ((relCurveMap C R R').base z) hfzy).hom
   293	            (d.eqn ((relCurveMap C R R').base y)))) := by
   294	    rw [hgermF, hdecomp, map_mul, IsUnit.unit_spec]
   295	  rw [hgermG]
   296	  have hSM : ((relCurveMap C R R').stalkMap z).hom
   297	      (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   298	        (d.cover.opens ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))
   299	        ((relCurveMap C R R').base z) hfzy).hom
   300	        (d.eqn ((relCurveMap C R R').base y))) =
   301	      ↑hunit.unit⁻¹ *
   302	        ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ
   303	          ((A.toFinCoverData.baseChange R').pieces j) z hzj).hom (A.pulledEqn R' j) := by
   304	    rw [hkey, ← mul_assoc, Units.inv_mul, one_mul]
   305	  rw [hSM]
   306	  exact mul_mem hunit.unit⁻¹.isUnit.mem_nonZeroDivisors hF
   307	
   308	/-- **The pulled local-equation system** on the relative curve over `R'`: `d` pulls back
   309	along the relative-curve comparison, with regularity discharged by the certificate's
   310	colength projectivity. -/
   311	noncomputable def pulledEquations (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)) :
   312	    (relCurve C R').LocalEquations :=
   313	  d.pullback (relCurveMap C R R') (A.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors R' hproj)
   314	
   315	@[simp]
   316	lemma pulledEquations_cover (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)) :
   317	    (A.pulledEquations R' hproj).cover = d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R') :=
   318	  rfl
   319	
   320	/-- The Picard class of the pulled system is the pullback of the class of `d`. -/
   321	lemma picClass_pulledEquations (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)) :
   322	    (A.pulledEquations R' hproj).picClass =
   323	      Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R R') d.picClass :=
   324	  Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_pullback (relCurveMap C R R') d _
   325	
   326	end DivisorAdaptation

   328	end AlgebraicGeometry

   110	/-- Basic opens of pinned-chart sections commute with relative base change, uniformly
   111	in the chosen side. -/
   112	lemma relPinnedSectionsMap_basicOpen
   113	    (L : Type u) [CommRing L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower k R L]
   114	    (b : Bool) (g : Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R pi b)) :
   115	    (relCurve C L).basicOpen (relPinnedSectionsMap C R L pi b g) =
   116	      relCurveMap C R L ⁻¹ᵁ (relCurve C R).basicOpen g := by
   117	  cases b with
   118	  | false => exact relSectionsMap_basicOpen C R L (fiberChart₀ pi) g
   119	  | true => exact relSectionsMap_basicOpen C R L (fiberChart₁ pi) g
   120	
   121	lemma relPinnedPieceSectionsMap_eq_appLE
   122	    (L : Type u) [CommRing L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower k R L]
   123	    (b : Bool) (g : Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R pi b))
   124	    (s : Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen g)) :
   125	    relPinnedPieceSectionsMap (C := C) (R := R) (pi := pi) L b g s =
   126	      ((relCurveMap C R L).appLE
   127	        ((relCurve C R).basicOpen g)
   128	        ((relCurve C L).basicOpen (relPinnedSectionsMap C R L pi b g))
   129	        (relPinnedSectionsMap_basicOpen (C := C) (R := R) (pi := pi) L b g).le).hom s := by
   130	  cases b <;> rfl

   132	namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed
   133	
   134	variable {D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R pi a K}
   135	
   136	/-- The seed's fibre-regularity clause on all basic subopens includes the whole piece. -/
   137	theorem eqn_tmul_one_mem_nonZeroDivisors (hD : D.IsGenerator)
   138	    (z : relCurve C R) (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
   139	    (D.eqn z ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ∈
   140	      nonZeroDivisors
   141	        (Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
   142	  exact tmul_one_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_eq p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   143	    (Scheme.basicOpen_one (X := relCurve C R) (U := D.piece z)).symm (D.eqn z)
   144	    (hD.fibre_regular z p (1 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z)))
   145	
   146	variable [IsNoetherianRing R]
   147	
   148	/-- The pullback of the seed local equation to a residue-field fibre is regular at its
   149	own indexed point.  The whole-piece tensor regularity is carried through the affine
   150	basic-open base-change equivalence, then compared with `pullbackEqn` by restriction
   151	naturality. -/
   152	theorem germ_self_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors (hD : D.IsGenerator)
   153	    (p : PrimeSpectrum R) (z : relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   154	    ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).presheaf.germ
   155	      (((D.localEquations hD).cover.pullback
   156	        (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField)).opens z) z
   157	      (((D.localEquations hD).cover.pullback
   158	        (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField)).mem_opens z)).hom
   159	      (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn
   160	        (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField) (D.localEquations hD) z) ∈
   161	      nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).presheaf.stalk z) := by
   162	  let y : relCurve C R := (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField).base z
   163	  have hseed := D.eqn_tmul_one_mem_nonZeroDivisors hD y p
   164	  have hcomm := map_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   165	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.comm R
   166	      Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece y) p.asIdeal.ResidueField).toRingEquiv hseed
   167	  change (Algebra.TensorProduct.comm R
   168	      Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece y) p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   169	      (D.eqn y ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ∈
   170	        nonZeroDivisors
   171	          (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece y)) at hcomm
   172	  rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.comm_tmul] at hcomm
   173	  have hpulled := map_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   174	    (relPinnedPieceBaseChange (C := C) (R := R) (pi := pi)
   175	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField (D.side y) (D.h y)).toRingEquiv hcomm
   176	  change relPinnedPieceBaseChange (C := C) (R := R) (pi := pi)
   177	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField (D.side y) (D.h y)
   178	      ((1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[R] D.eqn y) ∈
   179	        nonZeroDivisors
   180	          Γ(relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
   181	            (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).basicOpen
   182	              (relPinnedSectionsMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField pi
   183	                (D.side y) (D.h y))) at hpulled
   184	  rw [relPinnedPieceBaseChange_one_tmul] at hpulled
   185	  have hopen := relPinnedSectionsMap_basicOpen (C := C) (R := R) (pi := pi)
   186	    p.asIdeal.ResidueField (D.side y) (D.h y)
   187	  have hzW : z ∈ (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).basicOpen
   188	      (relPinnedSectionsMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField pi (D.side y) (D.h y)) := by
   189	    rw [hopen]
   190	    exact (D.localEquations hD).cover.mem_opens y
   191	  have hgerm := IsAffineOpen.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   192	    ((isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C p.asIdeal.ResidueField pi (D.side y)).basicOpen
   193	      (relPinnedSectionsMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField pi (D.side y) (D.h y)))
   194	    hpulled z hzW
   195	  have hres : (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).resHom hopen.le
   196	      (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn
   197	        (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField) (D.localEquations hD) z) =
   198	      relPinnedPieceSectionsMap (C := C) (R := R) (pi := pi)
   199	        p.asIdeal.ResidueField (D.side y) (D.h y) (D.eqn y) := by
   200	    calc
   201	      _ = ((relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField).appLE
   202	          ((relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h y))
   203	          ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).basicOpen
   204	            (relPinnedSectionsMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField pi
   205	              (D.side y) (D.h y))) hopen.le).hom (D.eqn y) :=
   206	        Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn_res
   207	          (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField) (D.localEquations hD) z hopen.le
   208	      _ = _ := (relPinnedPieceSectionsMap_eq_appLE
   209	        (C := C) (R := R) (pi := pi) p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   210	        (D.side y) (D.h y) (D.eqn y)).symm
   211	  rw [← hres] at hgerm
   212	  have hgres := TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply
   213	    (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).presheaf (homOfLE hopen.le) z hzW
   214	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn
   215	      (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField) (D.localEquations hD) z)
   216	  change ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).presheaf.germ
   217	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).basicOpen
   218	        (relPinnedSectionsMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField pi
   219	          (D.side y) (D.h y))) z hzW).hom
   220	      (((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).presheaf.map
   221	        (homOfLE hopen.le).op).hom
   222	        (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn
   223	          (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField) (D.localEquations hD) z)) ∈
   224	      nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).presheaf.stalk z) at hgerm
   225	  rw [hgres] at hgerm
   226	  exact hgerm

    10	/-!
    11	# Fibre regularity for an adaptation extracted from a theta-generator seed
    12	
    13	The certificate assembler requires each adaptation equation to remain regular on every
    14	residue-field fibre.  This file transports the corresponding `ThetaGeneratorSeed`
    15	property through the extracted local-equation system and the adaptation's pointwise
    16	`eqn_rel` units, without assuming any colength certificate.
    17	-/
    18

    32	/-- A ring equivalence carries nonzerodivisors to nonzerodivisors. -/
    33	private lemma map_mem_nonZeroDivisors {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    34	    (e : A ≃+* B) {x : A} (hx : x ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) :
    35	    e x ∈ nonZeroDivisors B := by
    36	  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff] at hx ⊢
    37	  obtain ⟨hl, hr⟩ := hx
    38	  constructor
    39	  · intro y hy
    40	    have h := congrArg e.symm hy
    41	    rw [map_mul, map_zero, e.symm_apply_apply] at h
    42	    have hy0 : e.symm y = 0 := hl _ h
    43	    calc y = e (e.symm y) := (e.apply_symm_apply y).symm
    44	      _ = 0 := by rw [hy0, map_zero]
    45	  · intro y hy
    46	    have h := congrArg e.symm hy
    47	    rw [map_mul, map_zero, e.symm_apply_apply] at h
    48	    have hy0 : e.symm y = 0 := hr _ h
    49	    calc y = e (e.symm y) := (e.apply_symm_apply y).symm
    50	      _ = 0 := by rw [hy0, map_zero]
    51	
    52	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    53	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    54	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi] {a : Nat}
    55	variable {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R pi a)}
    56	
    57	/-- The side-uniform piece-sections base-change equivalence on a pinned chart. -/
    58	noncomputable def relPinnedPieceBaseChange
    59	    (L : Type u) [CommRing L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower k R L]
    60	    (b : Bool) (g : Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R pi b)) :
    61	    L ⊗[R] Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen g) ≃ₐ[L]
    62	      Γ(relCurve C L,
    63	        (relCurve C L).basicOpen (relPinnedSectionsMap C R L pi b g)) :=
    64	  match b with
    65	  | false =>
    66	      pieceTermBaseChangeAlg L (fiberChart₀ pi)
    67	        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₀.isCompact
    68	        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₀.isQuasiSeparated
    69	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover pi))
    70	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C L (fiberTwoCover pi)) g

     9	/-!
    10	# Reading compatibility at a residue-field point
    11	
    12	The chart comparison map is defined by the scheme `appLE`.  This file records its
    13	stalk form, and then combines it with the universal-window comparison.  The latter
    14	is the pointwise bridge used by the single-point RD-N argument: a total-space reading
    15	transported to `κ(p)` and germed at the canonical lift of `z` is the germ of the
    16	`windowCompare` fibre reading.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    21	
    22	universe u
    23	
    24	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    25	open Opposite
    26	open scoped TensorProduct
    27	
    28	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    29	
    30	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    31	
    32	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    33	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    34	variable (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R']
    35	  [IsScalarTower k R R']
    36	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
    37	
    38	/-! ## Stalk form of the chart comparison -/
    39	
    40	/-- The germ of a section after the relative-curve comparison is the image of the
    41	germ at the image point under the induced stalk map. -/
    42	theorem relPinnedSectionsMap_germ_eq_stalkMap
    43	    (b : Bool) {s : Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)}
    44	    {z : relCurve C R'} (hz : z ∈ relPinnedChart C R' π b) :
    45	    ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ (relPinnedChart C R' π b) z hz).hom
    46	        (relPinnedSectionsMap C R R' π b s)
    47	      = ((relCurveMap C R R').stalkMap z).hom
    48	          (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (relPinnedChart C R π b)
    49	            ((relCurveMap C R R').base z)
    50	            (by
    51	              change z ∈ relCurveMap C R R' ⁻¹ᵁ relPinnedChart C R π b
    52	              rw [relCurveMap_preimage_relPinnedChart C R (π := π) b R']
    53	              exact hz)).hom s) := by
    54	  cases b with
    55	  | false =>
    56	      let f := relCurveMap C R R'
    57	      let U := relPinnedChart C R π false
    58	      let W := relPinnedChart C R' π false
    59	      let e : W ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U :=
    60	        le_of_eq (relCurveMap_preimage_relPinnedChart C R (π := π) false R').symm
    61	      have happ : relPinnedSectionsMap C R R' π false s =
    62	          (f.appLE U W e).hom s := by
    63	        rfl
    64	      rw [happ]
    65	      rw [show (f.appLE U W e).hom s =
    66	          ((relCurve C R').presheaf.map (homOfLE e).op).hom
    67	            ((f.app U).hom s) by rfl]
    68	      rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    69	      exact (f.germ_stalkMap_apply U z (e hz) s).symm
    70	  | true =>
    71	      let f := relCurveMap C R R'
    72	      let U := relPinnedChart C R π true
    73	      let W := relPinnedChart C R' π true
    74	      let e : W ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U :=
    75	        le_of_eq (relCurveMap_preimage_relPinnedChart C R (π := π) true R').symm
    76	      have happ : relPinnedSectionsMap C R R' π true s =
    77	          (f.appLE U W e).hom s := by
    78	        rfl
    79	      rw [happ]
    80	      rw [show (f.appLE U W e).hom s =
    81	          ((relCurve C R').presheaf.map (homOfLE e).op).hom
    82	            ((f.app U).hom s) by rfl]
    83	      rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    84	      exact (f.germ_stalkMap_apply U z (e hz) s).symm

    89	    (b : Bool) {z : relCurve C R'} (hz : z ∈ relPinnedChart C R' π b)
    90	    (s : Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)) :
    91	    relPinnedSectionsMap C R R' π b s ∈

   104	    (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π b).primeIdealOf_eq_map_closedPoint]
   105	  change ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ (relPinnedChart C R' π b) z hz).hom

   107	        IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R').presheaf.stalk z) ↔
   108	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (relPinnedChart C R π b)
   109	      ((relCurveMap C R R').base z) hzbase).hom s ∈

   111	          ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk ((relCurveMap C R R').base z))

   125	/-- At the canonical residue-field lift of a point `z`, the germ of the transported
   126	total universal-window reading is the germ of the fibre reading obtained by
   127	`windowCompare`. -/
   128	theorem germ_relPinnedSectionsMap_relThetaResSide_windowEquiv_at_relCurveResiduePoint
   129	    (b : Bool) {z : relCurve C R}
   130	    (hz : z ∈ relPinnedChart C R π b)
   131	    (x : R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) :
   132	    let K := (relCurveBasePoint C R z).asIdeal.ResidueField
   133	    let zK := relCurveResiduePoint C R z
   134	    ((relCurve C K).presheaf.germ (relPinnedChart C K π b) zK
   135	      (relCurveResiduePoint_mem_relPinnedChart C R (π := π) b hz)).hom
   136	      (relPinnedSectionsMap C R K π b
   137	        (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl (relThetaWindowEquiv C R π a hH1 x)))
   138	      = ((relCurve C K).presheaf.germ (relPinnedChart C K π b) zK
   139	          (relCurveResiduePoint_mem_relPinnedChart C R (π := π) b hz)).hom
   140	        (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl
   141	          (relThetaWindowEquiv C K π a hH1 (windowCompare R K x))) := by
   142	  dsimp
   143	  exact congrArg
   144	    (((relCurve C (relCurveBasePoint C R z).asIdeal.ResidueField).presheaf.germ
   145	      (relPinnedChart C (relCurveBasePoint C R z).asIdeal.ResidueField π b)
   146	      (relCurveResiduePoint C R z)
   147	      (relCurveResiduePoint_mem_relPinnedChart C R (π := π) b hz)).hom)
   148	    (relPinnedSectionsMap_relThetaResSide_windowEquiv C R
   149	      (relCurveBasePoint C R z).asIdeal.ResidueField π a hH1 b x)
   150	
   151	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
   152	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 500000 in
   153	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   154	/-- Stalk-map form of the residue-point reading comparison: the image of the total
   155	reading germ is exactly the germ of the `windowCompare` fibre reading. -/
   156	theorem stalkMap_germ_relThetaResSide_windowEquiv_at_relCurveResiduePoint
   157	    (b : Bool) {z : relCurve C R}
   158	    (hz : z ∈ relPinnedChart C R π b)
   159	    (x : R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) :
   160	    let K := (relCurveBasePoint C R z).asIdeal.ResidueField
   161	    let zK := relCurveResiduePoint C R z
   162	    ((relCurveMap C R K).stalkMap zK).hom
   163	        (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (relPinnedChart C R π b)
   164	          ((relCurveMap C R K).base zK)
   165	          (by
   166	            change zK ∈ relCurveMap C R K ⁻¹ᵁ relPinnedChart C R π b
   167	            rw [relCurveMap_preimage_relPinnedChart C R (π := π) b K]
   168	            exact relCurveResiduePoint_mem_relPinnedChart C R (π := π) b hz)).hom
   169	          (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl (relThetaWindowEquiv C R π a hH1 x)))
   170	      = ((relCurve C K).presheaf.germ (relPinnedChart C K π b) zK
   171	          (relCurveResiduePoint_mem_relPinnedChart C R (π := π) b hz)).hom
   172	        (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl
   173	          (relThetaWindowEquiv C K π a hH1 (windowCompare R K x))) := by
   174	  dsimp
   175	  rw [← relPinnedSectionsMap_germ_eq_stalkMap C R
   176	    (relCurveBasePoint C R z).asIdeal.ResidueField (π := π) b
   177	    (relCurveResiduePoint_mem_relPinnedChart C R (π := π) b hz)]
   178	  exact germ_relPinnedSectionsMap_relThetaResSide_windowEquiv_at_relCurveResiduePoint
   179	    C R (π := π) a hH1 b hz x
